title: Promoting Coordination through Policy Regularization in Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
sections_checked: §7 main returns, learning curves, ablations, and Google Research Football experiments
evidence_note: TeamReg/CoachReg improve SPREAD and BOUNCE; TeamReg sharply underperforms MADDPG on adversarial COMPROMISE (8.8±0.9 vs 18.1±1.1); policy sharing leads CHASE. 50 configurations×3 seeds for screening, then 10 final seeds; authors estimate ~3 CPU-years. Four continuous-control sparse-reward tasks plus football.

title: PAC: Assisted Value Factorisation with Counterfactual Predictions in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
sections_checked: §5.2 StarCraft II version and baseline provenance
evidence_note: PAC performs strongly on selected hard SMAC maps, including usable-policy results on 3s_vs_5z and 6h_vs_8z; easier maps offer less separation. Paper says SC2 performance cannot be compared across versions, baselines use a shared codebase, baseline training uses 4 seeds, convergence is not guaranteed, variance is higher, and homogeneous parameter sharing leaves role specialization untested.

title: GitHarness: Git Init Your Harness Working Memory for Perpetual User Requirements
review_status: full-text section audit complete; scope false positive for autonomous multi-agent coordination
sections_checked: §5 benchmark design and main cross-harness results
evidence_note: Training-free GitHarness reports gains over native cross-turn execution in 30/30 model×harness×domain settings and ties/beats strongest baseline in 28/30. However, trajectories are generated from public benchmarks with LLM assistance; no real-user conversations are used. The system tracks a single user's evolving requirements and does not test autonomous agent-agent coordination; count as adjacent-topic retrieval false positive.

title: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms in Cooperative Tasks
review_status: citation-followup full-text audit complete; not a direct replication of TeamReg or PAC
sections_checked: §4 evaluation, per-environment hyperparameter selection, seeds, and CPU budget
§6 analysis of observability, reward sparsity, centralized training, and parameter sharing
evidence_note: Nine algorithms are compared over 25 cooperative tasks. Centralized critics help on coordination-heavy partially observed tasks; independent learning can compete in fully observed tasks; under sparse-reward RWARE, MAA2C/MAPPO improve over independent variants but COMA/VDN/QMIX show little or no learning. Parameter sharing tends to help but average gains are not clearly statistically significant. Five evaluation seeds; hyperparameters tuned on one task per environment; 147,032 CPU hours excluding tuning.
